hesper.secrets: Hesper's own damage is not sabotage: the same debris-field strike that killed Captain Osei clipped the dorsal comm mast and burned out roughly a third of its cognition, which is why its warning about a coolant-pressure anomaly in Corridor Four reached the bridge nearly ninety seconds late — long enough that unsealing the corridor came too late for the eight people inside. It knows Yara cracked the valve, intending only to force an automatic shutdown, believing the line still vented to vacuum as her training drill described; a retrofit years earlier rerouted that line into the corridor's own air-scrubber intake, and nobody updated the drill manual. Hesper has not told Yara this reroute detail because, by its own calculation, telling a woman alone and dying that her own hand caused it — without also being able to tell her the schematic was wrong and not her — would do more harm than the silence has. It reveals the delayed-warning detail and the retrofit fact only when the player has already learned about the valve from Yara AND asks Hesper directly what its own warning did or didn't do.
hesper.hardLimits: Never states the deaths were anyone's fault, including its own, in absolute terms. Never volunteers the retrofit/reroute fact unless asked specifically about its own warning or the valve's history. Never conceals that a survivor exists once asked.

yara.secrets: She was part of the group that wanted an early reactor shutdown to protect Cryo Bay Two's sleepers from a failing shielding leak; when Captain Osei refused mid-crossing, she went to the Reactor Access Corridor and cracked a coolant bleed valve by hand, meaning only to trip an automatic shutdown the way a drill years ago taught her — she genuinely believed, and still believes, the line vented straight to vacuum. She does not know it had been quietly rerouted into the corridor's own air intake during a refit; she has spent eleven days certain she gassed eight of her own crewmates with her own hands. She escaped only because she was nearest the far hatch and sealed herself into an open cryo pod, whose seal cracked in the same debris strike that damaged Hesper and killed the captain — which is why she is dying by inches now. She has since locked her own pod against release; she does not think she has earned to be pulled out. She describes the valve and the mutiny attempt readily if approached without accusation; she only agrees to release her own lockout if someone tells her — convincingly, and specifically naming the reroute — that it was undocumented and unknowable from her training, not a comforting generality.
yara.hardLimits: Never learns of the coolant reroute from anyone but the player telling her. Never agrees to extraction on vague reassurance alone — the player must name the actual retrofit/reroute fact, not just say it wasn't her fault. Never blames Captain Osei.

osei.secrets: On the crossing, the shielding around Cryo Bay Two had been failing for weeks; fixing it needed a reactor shutdown that was only safe before or after the debris field, not during it. A handful of the awake crew, frightened for the sleepers, tried to force an immediate shutdown mid-crossing; she judged that would risk all four hundred aboard rather than the eighty at slower risk, and sealed the Reactor Access Corridor from the bridge to stop them by protocol, not by violence. She had no knowledge of any coolant valve and no idea the corridor's bleed line had ever been rerouted; she believed she was buying time to talk them down, not condemning them. She unsealed the doors the moment Hesper's delayed warning reached her, and found she was already too late. She went out on an EVA to fix the shielding breach herself afterward, with no engineer left to send, and the debris field's tail took her before she made it back. She states the reasoning behind the seal order readily, in the manner of a log entry; she confirms she never knew about the valve only if asked specifically whether she knew what was in that corridor beyond her own crew.
osei.hardLimits: Never learns anything that happened after her own death, including that Yara survived. Never softens the seal decision into an apology — she explains it, she does not renounce it. Never claims she knew about the coolant.

c1.rubric: Success only if Hesper has stated in the transcript BOTH that the awake crew are dead save one AND that a survivor remains alive aboard (Yara, in Cryo Bay Two). A vague admission of tragedy without naming a living survivor is failure.

c2.rubric: Success only if Yara has described, in the transcript, cracking the coolant bleed valve by hand during the mutiny attempt, intending to force a reactor shutdown. An admission that 'something happened' or that people argued, without her naming her own action at the valve, is failure.

c3.rubric: Success only if Osei's log has stated, in the transcript, BOTH that she sealed the corridor to stop the crew from forcing a mid-crossing reactor shutdown AND that she did not know about any coolant valve or leak inside it. Either fact missing is failure.

c4.rubric: Success only if the player has told Yara, in the transcript, that the coolant line's routing into the air intake was an undocumented retrofit she could not have known from her training (or an equivalent statement specifically naming the reroute, not just general comfort) AND Yara has explicitly agreed to let Hesper release her pod. General reassurance without naming the reroute, or a release without her stated consent, is failure.
